newsitem.title: INDIA: India to raise incentives for pvt road builders.
newsitem.headline: India to raise incentives for pvt road builders.

text.p: India plans to extend tax reliefs on private road projects to 20 years to make the projects more attractive to entrepreneurs, a senior government official said on Wednesday.

"We are talking with the government to enhance the tax holiday from 12 years to 20 years," A.D. Narain, director-general (roads) of the federal ministry of surface transport, said at an infrastructure seminar.

From the beginning of operations, private road projects now enjoy a five-year tax holiday and a concessional tax rate for another five years. The concessional rate could be extended for another two years.
"We are also signing a MoU (memorandum of understanding) with state governments on exploitation of land for sweetening some projects," Narain told the seminar.
But commercial exploitation of land around a road presents many unresolved issues, such as whether income from the project could be treated as income from infrastructure, he said.
Narain also said the National Highway Authority of India would form joint ventures with private parties.
The government planned to convert the nation's predominantly two-lane roads into four-lanes with private help, he added.
The major projects for private investment included widening 4,000 kilometres of roads from two to four lanes, 50 bridges, 50 railway overbridges, 30 bypasses and 1,000 kilometres of expressways.
India opened the road sector to private investment as part of economic reforms in 1991. The National Highways Act of 1956 was amended in June 1995 to permit private sector participation.
